about: The held-pose rule (A11): src/domain/orientation/orientation.ts classify() and track(), and HeldPose.classify and PoseTracker (Kotlin), pass every row and every track; JS ignores side. g is gravity in g; physical null is the dead band. side is native's alone: left is the phone's top to the left (gravity along +x, ROTATION_90), right the other way round (ROTATION_270), a hypothesis until the device gate reads the encoded picture upright both ways round (P4). The edge rows sit 1e-9 either side of each comparison, in the quantity compared (g, degrees, or the share of gravity through the screen): far above rounding (about 1e-16) and below a float32 sensor's step (about 6e-8 at 1 g), so any correct float maths classifies them alike. Which side a reading exactly on 0.94, 0.87, 30 or 60 degrees falls is deliberately not pinned: engines may round it either way. The floor row at exactly 0.3 g is single-axis, where the magnitude is exactly 0.3 under any correct float maths, so it does pin the floor's comparison. holdMs is HOLD_MS on both sides. Each track starts from nothing settled; settled and side are the tracker's settled reading after each step. Change only with both.

tracks.why: a reading settles at exactly holdMs, not a millisecond before
a dip into the dead band restarts the hold: it runs from the reading after the dip
a swing through the dead band to upright settles upright after its own hold
turning to the other side: JS stays landscape, native settles the new side after the hold
laid flat after being held sideways
no gravity is a reading that settles unknown, unlike the dead band
the dead band alone never settles anything
a dip into the dead band, then no gravity: unknown settles a full hold after its own first reading
